Moving the remaining contour to Re(s)=c>1 exposes the pole at s=1-ia in the full case; horizontal and vertical estimates control the remainder uniformly in a. Substituting the earlier divisor-sum asymptotic gives the two zeta main terms, while replacing the shifted factor by zeta_N removes the pole and leaves the zeta_N(1+ia) term.
directed.conceptual_reading: The proof changes representation twice: the functional equation changes a line correlation into a chi-weighted Dirichlet series, and contour displacement separates coefficient mass from singularity data. This makes the dual main term legible as a residue rather than as an unexplained feature of the moment formula; analyticity of the truncated factor then explains why that term disappears.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge objects are the generalized divisor coefficients sigma_{-ia}(n), their partial sums D_{ia}(x) and D_{ia}(x;N), the chi-kernel integral of Lemma A.4, and the pole crossed during the contour shift.
